title: Core components
summary: How React Native renders real native views: View, Text, Image, TextInput, Pressable and ScrollView, and how they differ from DOM elements.

sections.title: React, but not the DOM
sections.body:
React Native uses the same React: components, props, state, hooks and reconciliation all work as on the web. What changes is the host. Instead of `div` and `span`, you render host components such as `View` and `Text`, and the renderer turns them into real platform views (a `UIView` on iOS, an `android.view.View` on Android).

There is no HTML, no CSS cascade and no `document`. Anything you know about React itself carries over; anything that relied on the browser does not.

sections.title: The everyday components
sections.body:
- `View`: a layout container, like a `div`. It cannot hold raw text.
- `Text`: the only component that renders strings. Nested `Text` inherits font styles from its parent `Text`.
- `Image`: local (`require('./logo.png')`) or remote (`{ uri }`) images. Remote images need an explicit width and height.
- `TextInput`: a text field, usually controlled with `value` and `onChangeText`.
- `Pressable`: the modern touch wrapper with `onPress`, `onLongPress` and a `pressed` state for styling.
- `ScrollView`: scrolls all of its children, which are all rendered at once.

sections.title: Text rules
sections.body:
Every string must sit inside `<Text>`. Rendering `{count}` or `{'hi'}` directly inside a `View` is an error ("Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component"). A common trap is `{items.length && <List />}`: when the length is `0`, React renders the number `0` as a string outside `Text` and the app crashes. Use `items.length > 0 &&` instead.

Styles like `color` and `fontSize` only inherit inside a `Text` tree, never from a `View`.

sections.title: Touch and input
sections.body: `onPress` replaces `onClick`. `TextInput` gives you `onChangeText(text)` with the new string rather than an event, plus `onSubmitEditing`, `keyboardType`, `secureTextEntry` and `autoCapitalize`. Wrap forms in `KeyboardAvoidingView` (or adjust insets) so the keyboard does not cover the focused field.

pitfalls: Rendering a raw string or number inside a `View`.
Using `&&` with a number that can be `0`.
Forgetting width and height on a remote `Image`, so it renders at zero size.
Using `ScrollView` for long, dynamic lists instead of a virtualised list.

gotchas.question: What happens with this code when `unread` is `0`?
gotchas.answer: React renders `0`, a string, directly inside a `View`, which throws "Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component". Use `unread > 0 && ...` or a ternary.

gotchas.question: Does `color: 'red'` on a `View` make the `Text` inside it red?
gotchas.answer: No. React Native has no style cascade. Only `Text` passes text styles to nested `Text` children.

gotchas.question: What does `onChangeText` receive?
gotchas.answer: The new text as a string. `onChange` receives a native event whose `nativeEvent.text` holds the same string.
